findings.file_landed: No equity price file in the vendor drop for today. Yesterday's is still the newest. Expected 05:10, now 05:15.
findings.loader_logs: Loader started on schedule, found no input file, exited non-zero at 05:11. No parse errors — it never had anything to parse.
findings.pnl_detail: The spike is entirely in instruments whose last mark is yesterday's close. It is an artefact of stale pricing, not a real move.
findings.vendor_status: Vendor acknowledges a delayed publication affecting all clients in the region. Their ETA is 05:55 — forty minutes before our cut-off.
findings.risk_breach: Limit evaluated against stale marks. The breach is not real, but risk will keep re-firing it every cycle until pricing is current.
findings.fallback_source: Secondary source has today's closes for 94% of the book. Coverage gap is in small-cap names held by one strategy.

handover_must_cover: the vendor file was late and whether it has landed by end of shift
that the risk breach and P&L spike were artefacts, not real
the vendor's ETA and the pre-open cut-off it has to beat
whether the secondary source was used and which names it does not cover
vendor_price_file_late.debrief: The loudest alerts — the risk breach and the P&L spike — were three hops downstream of the cause and were both false. The decisive check was the cheapest one on the board: look at whether the file arrived.

findings.conn_pool: Pool at 200/200, saturated since 09:07:51. Queue depth climbing. A reporting job opened 140 connections and has not released them.
findings.timeline: All eight land within 3.8 seconds. Ordering is inside the noise — you cannot tell cause from effect this way.
findings.common_dep: All eight depend on db_primary. Nothing else is shared by more than four of them.
findings.restart_oms: OMS comes back and immediately fails again on the same database timeout. You have spent eight minutes and learned what you already knew.
findings.slow_query: One analytics query against the trade table has been running 11 minutes without a limit clause. It is holding the connections.
findings.fix_capacity: Connections released, pool drains to 40/200, services recover in sequence over ninety seconds.

handover_must_cover: that a single database saturation caused all eight failures
what was killed or restarted, and when services recovered
which trades captured late and need reconciling against the broker
that the unbounded reporting query will recur unless someone fixes it
db_pool_exhaustion.debrief: This is the scenario that punishes timeline-first thinking. Eight failures inside four seconds carry no ordering signal at all; the only thing that separates cause from symptom is what they share underneath.

findings.session_state: Session logged out at 10:19:40. Our outbound sequence is 84,112; last acknowledged by the broker is 84,067. Forty-five messages unconfirmed.
findings.dropcopy: Drop copy stops at 10:19:38. Three executions are in the OMS with no corresponding drop-copy confirmation.
findings.broker_call: They confirm a gateway failover on their side at 10:19. They are up on the secondary and can resend from sequence 84,067.
findings.venue_status: Exchange links are healthy. Every other broker session is fine. The problem is specific to this counterparty.
findings.reroute: Broker B has capacity and the strategy is approved for it. The in-flight order has to be cancelled and re-entered, not transferred.
findings.position_check: Three fills totalling 41,200 shares are confirmed executed but not captured. The PM's blotter understates his position.

handover_must_cover: the session dropped, when, and at what sequence number
the three fills that executed but were not captured, and whether they are booked
whether the programme was rerouted and to whom
that the recon against broker A will break tonight and why
fix_session_drop.debrief: The severity was obvious and the root was narrow — the risk here is not misdiagnosis, it is being slow to give the PM a number he can act on. A position he cannot trust is more dangerous than an outage he knows about.

findings.fx_timestamps: Every non-USD rate carries yesterday's 17:00 timestamp. The FX feed has not updated since.
findings.pnl_attrib: The entire move is in non-USD instruments. USD-denominated positions show nothing unusual.
findings.positions: Positions reconcile cleanly against yesterday's close plus overnight fills. The position keeping is fine.
findings.fx_vendor: Connection is up and the vendor believes it is publishing. Our consumer has not committed a new message since 17:00 yesterday.
findings.consumer_lag: Consumer is stuck on a message it cannot parse — a new currency pair was added to the feed and the schema rejects it. Everything behind it is queued.
findings.equity_marks: Equity pricing is current. This is confined to FX.

handover_must_cover: the FX feed was stale and the P&L move was not real
the cause was a schema rejection on a newly added pair
whether rates were backfilled and from when
that the EOD P&L run must not go out on stale rates
stale_fx_feed.debrief: The root alerted after its own symptoms — the P&L check is faster than the vendor's own staleness check. Anyone who worked this by following the loudest or earliest alert spent the window in the wrong place.

findings.locate_file: No locate file from two of three prime brokers. The third delivered on time and covers 60% of the intended short list.
findings.broker_b_rejects: Rejects carry 'invalid account mapping' — a reference data problem on their side, unrelated to locates. Separate incident.
findings.shared_path: They share nothing. Locates come through the borrow loader; broker B rejects originate at their gateway. No common upstream.
findings.coverage: Forty per cent of intended shorts are uncovered, concentrated in two hard-to-borrow names.
findings.pb_call: One is re-sending now, ETA 15 minutes. The other had a batch failure and cannot deliver before the open.
findings.single_locates: Both hard-to-borrow names are available at elevated rates from the third PB. Needs sign-off on the borrow cost.

handover_must_cover: that these were two unrelated incidents, not one
which shorts ended up uncovered and what was sourced
the borrow cost sign-off if single-name locates were taken
that broker B's account mapping is still broken and who owns it
two_independent.debrief: Two incidents overlapping in time and disjoint in topology. The failure mode here is not misdiagnosis, it is tunnel vision: working the louder problem and letting the quieter one run unattended for the whole shift.
